$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. ThreadMarker realizes THREAD_TOPOLOGY_PLAN.md's 'Data model' §`thread_markers` table (id, rootId, anchorMsgId?, kind CHAPTER|SESSION_START|COMPACTION_RUN|LINEAGE_SRC, label?, note?, at, source USER|SYSTEM, payloadJson?), carried as a ContractEnvelope<ThreadMarker> payload per FB-RAT-COM-011 the same way ErrorEnvelope is (schemas/common/envelope.schema.json). A ThreadMarker is a RETROACTIVE fact about the append-only message tree (THREAD_TOPOLOGY_PLAN.md binding constraint 5: 'metadata minted at insert, never edited; retroactive facts -> Room tables') — it never mutates MessageNode.metadata, it lives in its own store (dev.aarso.data.ThreadMarkerStore). Field names here match the plan's own column-list naming verbatim (`at`, not `atUtc`/`createdAtUtc`) since this schema documents that exact table's wire shape, not a fresh contract inventing its own vocabulary.
title: ThreadMarker
description: A user- or system-placed marker on the conversation tree: a chapter boundary, a fresh-session start, a compaction-run boundary, or a lineage source pointer (fork/spawn origin). Created after the fact — the anchored message already exists — never edited in place except by the owning UI's own rename/remove actions on the marker row itself (the anchored MessageNode is never touched).

schemaVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH of this record's shape. A reader MUST reject an unrecognized MAJOR (FB-RAT-COM-003).

id.description: Globally unique stable id for this marker (FB-RAT-COM-002), independent of its label or anchor.

rootId.description: The conversation root this marker belongs to (dev.aarso.domain.tree.Conversations.Summary.rootId) — every marker is scoped to exactly one conversation, never shared across roots.

anchorMsgId.description: The message node this marker anchors to, when it anchors to one at all. Required non-null for CHAPTER (a chapter boundary IS a specific message). Null is valid for SESSION_START (a session boundary may mark 'start fresh from here forward' without naming a prior message) and for COMPACTION_RUN/LINEAGE_SRC when the marker instead points into `payloadJson` for its own reference shape (those two kinds are populated by later work packages — WP3's compaction runs, WP2's fork/spawn lineage — this schema only fixes the shared envelope, not their payload internals).

kind.description: THREAD_TOPOLOGY_PLAN.md's four marker kinds, verbatim. CHAPTER/SESSION_START are user-facing (TurnActionsSheet's 'Mark chapter here…'/'Start fresh session here'); COMPACTION_RUN/LINEAGE_SRC are system-facing, written by later work packages (WP3, WP2) reusing this same table rather than inventing a second one.

label.description: Required non-blank for CHAPTER (the user-entered chapter name, same naming-dialog pattern as dev.aarso.domain.curation.Version.name). Null for the other three kinds — SESSION_START/COMPACTION_RUN/LINEAGE_SRC are self-describing by `kind` alone and don't prompt for a name.

at.description: UTC instant this marker was created (FB-RAT-COM-004). This is when the MARKER was placed, which for a retroactive chapter mark is typically later than the anchored message's own timestamp — the two are independent clocks on purpose.

source.description: USER for anything placed through a TurnActionsSheet action; SYSTEM for anything written by an automated process (a future compaction run boundary, a fork/spawn operation recording its own lineage source marker).

payloadJson.description: Opaque per-kind JSON, mirroring dev.aarso.domain.mirror.AarsoEvent.payloadJson's 'the writer knows the shape' split — this schema does not need to understand a payload's internal shape to carry it. Encoded as a JSON string (not a nested object) because the owning kind's schema (e.g. a future COMPACTION_RUN receipt shape) is versioned independently of ThreadMarker itself.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).
